newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Wall Street depresses Europe bourses again.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Wall Street depresses Europe bourses again.

text.p: European stock markets fell on Monday as Wall Street investors went profit-taking again, while company tax hikes aimed at cutting the French budget deficit for European monetary union gave the Paris bourse an extra headache.
German shares leapt in early trading after news of a major bank merger but the market soon succumbed to the trend sweeping the continent.
Wall Street's heavy fall on Friday, as investors cashed in on the Dow Jones Industrial Average's brief trip over 8,000 points, triggered European selling at the opening.
The picture was similar, although less extreme, when New York opened lower on Monday and after half an hour's trade the Dow was down 23.23 points at 7,867.23.

Wall Street was undoubtedly the major depressant of the day but Paris had problems of its own as the new Socialist-led government tried to narrow the budget deficit towards the 3.0 percent of gross domestic product needed to qualify for European economic and monetary union (EMU).

Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn announced the government would cut the deficit by 32 billion francs ($5.3 billion) with 22 billion in higher taxes on companies' profits and capital gains and 10 billion in spending cuts.
This followed an audit of state finances which estimated that the public deficit would be 3.5 to 3.7 percent of GDP this year.
But much of the announcement had been leaked in general terms and the reaction on the Paris bourse was muted.
The CAC-40 index was off the day's lows, down 22.12 points (0.77 percent) at 2,854.57, by mid afternoon and retail stocks went up on relief that personal income tax had not been raised.
London's fall was motivated by Wall Street and by mid afternoon the FTSE-100 index of blue chips was down 70.1 points or 1.44 percent at 4,807.1.

"There is a bit of profit-taking and the buyers are holding off for the time being," said the head of market-making at one brokerage. "To try to guess the market's direction at the moment is impossible."
London dealers were also nervous about the Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Tuesday when Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan will report to Congress on the state of the U.S. economy.

Greenspan sent stock markets plunging around the world last December when he warned investors against irrational exuberance. Since then the bull run has resumed with a vengeance, pushing the Dow briefly through 8,000 points last week before the profit-takers cashed in.
"There are a few people out there talking about a 20 percent fall on Wall Street but the same people have been predicting that sort of move for a while now," said one head trader in London.

Frankfurt told a different story in early trade. The IBIS index of electronic trade jumped around 80 points to a high of 4,211.67 on news that two of Germany's largest commercial banks, Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypobank, would merge.
But the mood did not last and by early afternoon the IBIS was down 16.24 points at 4,115.70.

The DAX index of floor trade was disrupted by computer problems but later closed down 88.13 points or 2.1 percent to 4,108.40. Its fall, also prompted by Friday's dip in the dollar below 1.79 marks, was exaggerated as the DAX closed for the weekend before the Dow tumbled.
The dollar eased a little on the foreign exchanges after earlier gains. It was at 1.7952 marks and 115.70 yen, compared with 1.7892 and 115.35 in late trading on Friday.

The news from Paris had little effect. "Most of the damage has been done in anticipation of it. The government will have prepared the market for the worst," said Tim Fox, international economist at Standard Chartered.
The mark eased slightly to 3.3762 francs from 3.3805 late on Friday and a high of 3.3810 early on Monday.
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7952 marks and 115.70 yen, compared with 1.7892 and 115.35 in late trading on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1100 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 70.1 points or 1.44 percent at 4,807.1.
FRANKFURT - The IBIS index of electronic trade was down 16.24 points at 4,115.70. The DAX index of floor trade closed down 88.13 points or 2.1 percent at 4,108.40.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 22.12 points (0.77 percent) at 2,854.57.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $326.20 in the afternoon after closing at $324.15 an ounce on Friday. Silver was down one cent at $4.29. ($ = 6.041 French Francs)
